description: Validates backup verification jobs for non-production restore targets, defined verification queries, result artifact paths, schedule/trigger configuration, and failure alerting

rules.description: backup-verify-spec.json must exist, be valid JSON, and declare backupSource, restoreTarget, and verifyQueries
restoreTarget must not be production, prod, live, or prd unless productionOverride: true is set. Restoring a backup into production as a verification step risks data corruption and service disruption
rules.note: Override with productionOverride: true only with written justification

rules.description: verifyQueries must be a non-empty array. Without queries, the job can only verify that the restore process completed without error — it cannot confirm data integrity. A backup that restores silently with zero rows is not a valid backup
resultArtifactPath must be declared so the verification outcome is written to a known, retrievable location. Without a result path, verification failures cannot be reviewed after the job completes
The job must declare either a cron schedule or an event trigger so it runs automatically rather than only on demand. Manual-only verification means backups go untested until someone remembers
backup-verify-spec.json must not contain TODO, FIXME, HACK, XXX, or PLACEHOLDER markers

Failed verifications must trigger an alert (notifyOnFailure: true or alertChannel declared). An owner must be declared for on-call routing. A backup that cannot be restored is not a backup — silent failures are unacceptable

constraints.failure-notification: notifyOnFailure: true or alertChannel must be declared
